_comment: P3-4 (RC-25) — the standing Albanian/Gheg fluency baseline.
TWO NUMBERS, AND THEY ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. The remediation plan says 'baselined at
54/100', and 54 is the audit's WEIGHTED COMPOSITE across six dimensions (WF-E:
0.10*65 response-quality + 0.10*30 consistency = 53.5). Most of that composite is retrieval
and classification, which judge.ts does not measure at all.
What judge.ts DOES measure — register, dialect fit, grammar, encoding integrity of a
generated Albanian reply — is the 'Response quality (Albanian output)' dimension, scored 65.
So 65 is the number a re-score is comparable to; 54 is recorded because the plan names it and
because the composite is what 'the Gheg eval improves' ultimately refers to. Comparing a judge
run against 54 would flatter it by ~11 points for free.
HOW TO ADD A POINT: run `npm run eval:fluency -- --rescore <replies.jsonl>` against a batch of
DELIVERED assistant replies (not corpus utterances — those are the customers' own words and
score high by construction), then append to `history` with its date and what changed. Never
overwrite a point; the trend is the artefact.
NOT A GATE. LLM-judge verdicts are stochastic and cost money per run, so this never blocks a
merge — RC-25 is explicit that dialect CLASSIFICATION is a discrete label checkable without a
judge (that half is in ghegCorpus.test.ts, in CI) and that the judge is reserved for FLUENCY of
the generated reply. Trend over threshold.

comparable.notes: What judge.ts measures. Deductions: delivered mojibake (EV-011); Albanian-only hardcoded append on English conversations.

composite.notes: The headline number the remediation plan cites. Dominated by retrieval (35) and consistency (30), neither of which the fluency judge touches. The audit states a +/-10 honest band on this total.
